title: A retired row eats a middot from its findings

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`render_row` folds a retired item's reason into the findings cell:

    findings = f"{item.findings} {MIDDOT} {item.reason}".strip(f" {MIDDOT}")

`str.strip` takes a **set of characters**, not a suffix, so it removes any leading or
trailing run of spaces and middots from the whole joined string — reaching into text the
user wrote at either end:

    findings '· F1' + reason 'superseded'    ->  'F1 · superseded'    (leading · eaten)
    findings 'F1'   + reason 'superseded ·'  ->  'F1 · superseded'    (trailing · eaten)

The strip exists for the case where `findings` is empty, so the join would otherwise
render a leading `· `. That case deserves a conditional, not a character-set strip that
also reaches into content.

**Correction to this slice as filed.** It claimed a second symptom, a doubled separator
from `'F2 ·'` rendering as `'F2 · · superseded'`. That is not a bug and does not change:
the user wrote a trailing middot and the separator is added after it, so two is faithful.
The real defect is only the eaten text, and it is symmetric across both fields.

Only retired rows are affected, so it is small — but it is silent edits to someone's
text, which is the kind of thing a roadmap tool should never do.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Row_RetiredWithLeadingMiddotInFindings_KeepsIt`.
2. `Row_RetiredWithTrailingMiddotInFindings_DoesNotDoubleTheSeparator`.
3. `Row_RetiredWithNoFindings_ShowsOnlyTheReason` — the case the strip was for.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Join the parts that are actually present instead of stripping afterwards:
`" · ".join(p for p in (item.findings, item.reason) if p)`. That handles the empty case
by construction and never touches content.

**Not in this slice:** whether a reason belongs in the findings column at all. It does,
for the reason the existing comment gives — the status column alone does not say why.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: All three rows in the Why section render as written.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit, likely alongside the other.
